title: Correct word-census parity budgets; 22 <= f(7) <= 24 in the PR943 model
body:
The word-census engines in #2542/#2634/#2691 use bit-0 state groups with budgets derived for Hamming-weight parity. This can falsely prune universal words: the simple balanced n=4, L=8 word `01021323` covers all 16 masks but has bit-0 excess 8 against the incorrectly substituted budget 5. Historical count agreement therefore did not establish the claimed exclusions.

Adds an isolated corrective package with a weight-parity, revisit-aware C engine, proofs for both necessary collision budgets, independent direct/brute Python controls, and full fresh enumerations:

| L | weight split | nodes | universal |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
|20|(10,10)|590,371,593|0|
|20|(10,9)|244,301,902|0|
|20|(10,8)|14,450,133|0|
|20|(9,9)|67,643,567|0|
|20|(10,7)|35,241|0|
|18|(9,9)|951,416|0|

Each run completed from the empty prefix without a cap, exit 0, `complete=true`. Candidate leaves are not reported as all restored words. Exact split classification, parity-swap symmetry and padding of shorter restored words prove **22 <= f(7) <= 24 within the PR943 singleton prefix-walk model**; the known Gray length-24 witness is checked directly. No supplier, tariff, selected-frontier or kappa change. This is a finite computational exclusion, not a formal-kernel proof.

Validation: 164 small full-domain C/brute comparisons across four budget modes; 12 cap/input/output controls; 36 capped n=7 exact C/Python comparisons; independent mathematical checks; then a second complete six-case replay from the integrated package. Both production and integrated counts agree. The independent n=7 Python check is capped, not a second full n=7 implementation replay.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-weight-parity-census-correction/verify.py --full
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-weight-parity-census-correction --check-only
```

Observed: `PASS_F7_WEIGHT_PARITY_FULL ... f7_lower=22 f7_upper=24`; `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. ~1 minute for the C traversals on the recorded Apple arm64 host; standard-library Python 3.12 and Clang/GCC required. Quick mode runs fresh controls and checks stored receipts, and explicitly does not claim a fresh complete census.

Frozen predecessor packages are unchanged. Bit 0 remains valid in set-level searches using actual group sizes; later #2773/#2870/#2911/#2933/#2961 results are scoped separately in MATH.md. Also corrects the previous local session's overstrong “zero slack” implication. Scientific base a23bdc1b; refreshed main ec1f08b16 has unchanged pinned engines and selected record. No new competing correction found in the checked live PR/discussion corpus.

Continuation CLAIM: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691#issuecomment-6218443989 ; coordination: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18976359 .

Contributor: Nicholas Stone, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance including three complementary agents; no independent human review claimed. Credit Ross Richardson (PR943 model), Douglas Colkitt (PR1185 record), Aaron Wang/opencode (#2542/#2634 and later set-level work), Nicholas Stone (PR2691 predecessor engine). Apache-2.0. Open next questions: independent complete implementation replay and length 22 versus 24.
